suggested_titles.academic: Ontological Priority of Mathematical Structure Over Physical Reality: A Logical Argument
suggested_titles.provocative: The Universe Was Doing Math Before You Were Born
suggested_titles.series: DT-000: Foundational Claim — Math Before Matter

opening_analysis.diagnosis: The opening is exceptionally strong. The first sentence ('This paper was written by a man who believes in God') is a high-risk, high-reward hook that immediately signals honesty and defiance. The thesis appears clearly by paragraph 3 ('Mathematical structure is ontologically prior to physical reality'). The problem is visible from paragraph 1. The only weakness is that the opening may alienate secular readers before they reach the argument, but the author anticipates this and addresses it directly.

unresolved_tensions: The paper claims math is prior to matter but does not fully resolve what 'outside' means in Section 5 — the nature of the grounding entity is left ambiguous, which may frustrate readers seeking a complete ontology.

missing_bridges: Between Section 5 (limitation theorems) and Section 7 (falsification criteria) — Section 6 is missing, which may confuse readers expecting sequential numbering.
flow.suggested_reorder: No major reordering needed. Consider inserting a brief Section 6 that summarizes the argument before presenting falsification criteria, or renumber sections to avoid the gap.

paragraph_function_map.main_point: The author declares belief in God but asserts this should not disqualify the argument.
The author establishes his background and declares his beliefs, but states none appear in the paper.
Mathematical structure is ontologically prior to physical reality.
The Biaxiosum Rule: name your ground before critiquing another's.
Physicists use math as prior but avoid the ontological question.
The universe obeyed math for 13.8 billion years before humans existed.
Standard answers to the question fail examination.
Nominalism: math is invented.
The universe was counting before humans — nominalism fails.
Platonism: math is abstract.
Abstract objects cannot enforce compliance — Platonism fails.
Fictionalism: math is useful fiction.
False theories do not generate true predictions — fictionalism fails.
All three positions fail because they make math dependent on something else.
Asymmetry table shows mathematical truth has opposite properties to human invention.
The categorical mismatch proves math is not a human invention.
Temporal gap: 13.8 billion years of mathematical compliance without a mathematician.
The gap is the argument — simplest explanation is ontological priority.
Wigner's unreasonable effectiveness is explained by ontological priority.
Five limitation theorems converge: closed systems cannot certify themselves.

rearrangement_suggestions: Insert a Section 6 between Section 5 and Section 7 to summarize the argument before presenting falsification criteria, or renumber sections to avoid the gap.
Move the Biaxiosum Rule (paragraph 4) to an appendix or footnote to keep the opening focused on the argument.
Consider moving the 'Declared Position & Ground' section after the Central Claim to reduce initial reader resistance.
top_3_fixes: Fix the missing Section 6 — either insert a summary section or renumber to avoid the gap between Section 5 and Section 7.
Clarify what 'outside' means in Section 5 — the nature of the grounding entity is ambiguous and may weaken the argument for skeptical readers.
Add a brief conclusion paragraph that restates the central claim and its implications, as the paper currently ends abruptly with the burden framework.
